chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Suleiman ibn Rushayd, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Suleyman al-Daylami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the Children of Israel would begin (their meals) with vinegar and end with it, and we begin with salt and end with vinegar.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for starting and ending a meal according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a distinct prophetic etiquette (sunnah) for dining, contrasting the Jewish practice of using vinegar for both opening and closing meals with the Shia practice of beginning with salt and concluding with vinegar. Scholars interpret this not merely as a ritualistic difference but as a practical health guideline, noting that salt aids digestion at the start of a meal while vinegar helps settle the stomach and preserve food at the end, thereby reinforcing the Shia identity through daily bodily practices.
